Katanga Mining Ltd Announces Major Expansion at Congolese Copper-Cobalt Operations

LUBUMBASHI, Democratic Republic of the Congo, June 13 – Katanga Mining Ltd announced Thursday a significant investment to expand production capacity at its flagship copper-cobalt complex in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), aiming to reinforce its position as a leading supplier of critical battery minerals.

The company said the expansion, valued at $400 million, will boost annual copper production by 20% and cobalt output by 15% over the next two years. Construction work is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2024, with completion expected by late 2026.

“Our investment underscores our long-term confidence in the DRC as a premier mining jurisdiction,” said Katanga Mining Chief Executive Alain Tshisekedi in a statement. “We are committed to responsible growth that delivers value for our shareholders and benefits to local communities.”

The expansion project includes the installation of new milling equipment, an upgraded flotation circuit, and expanded tailings storage facilities. Katanga Mining will also construct a new workers’ camp and invest in community health and education initiatives as part of its social responsibility program.

Industry analysts say the move comes amid growing global demand for copper and cobalt—key metals in the transition to electric vehicles and renewable energy infrastructure. The DRC is the world’s largest producer of cobalt and accounts for more than 70% of global supply.

“Katanga’s decision is a strong signal of confidence in the sector’s fundamentals,” said Jean-Paul Mbuyi, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Resource Focus. “With electric vehicle production rising, demand for DRC cobalt is expected to remain robust for years to come.”

The expansion is expected to create approximately 1,200 temporary construction jobs and 300 permanent positions once operational. Local officials welcomed the announcement, citing the potential for increased tax revenues and economic activity in the Haut-Katanga province.

“This investment demonstrates the positive role responsible mining can play in Congo’s development,” said provincial mining director Marie-Louise Kabeya. “We look forward to working closely with Katanga Mining to ensure the benefits are widely shared.”

The Congolese Chamber of Mines said it supports initiatives that promote local hiring and sustainable development. “The mining industry is a pillar of the national economy,” said Chamber Secretary-General Joseph Mufuta. “Strategic investments like this help consolidate the DRC’s status as a global minerals powerhouse.”

Katanga Mining Ltd has operated in the region for more than two decades. The company said it will continue to engage with local stakeholders as the project advances.
